A comparison is a value of type bool : true (printed as 1) or false (0). Any non-zero number used as a condition counts as true, so if (n) means if (n != 0) .

Operator Meaning Example == != equal, not equal x % 2 == 0 (even) < <= > >= compare a <= b && and: both true 1 <= x && x <= 9 || or: at least one c == 'a' || c == 'A' ! not !(x > 5) a % b == 0 b divides a n % 3 == 0 Precedence, high to low: ! → arithmetic → < > → == != → && → || . Add brackets whenever you mix && and || .
Short-circuit: && stops at the first false part, || at the first true part. So n != 0 && a / n > 2 never divides by zero.
if (a = b) assigns instead of comparing. 1 < x < 5 means (1 < x) < 5 , which is always true. if (x); has an empty body. An else pairs with the nearest if : use braces.

title: if / else if / else, and switch

text: An else-if chain tests conditions in order and runs only the first that is true. Order matters: put the narrow cases first, or write each condition so it cannot overlap.
Normal
Underweight

Leap year: divisible by 4 and not by 100, or divisible by 400. switch works on integers and chars; each case needs break , or it falls through into the next case. The ? : operator picks between two values: x = cond ? a : b .

An if inside another if makes a decision tree: the inner question is only asked on one branch of the outer one. Draw the tree first when the cases depend on each other.
Braces show which else belongs to which if . Many nests can be flattened into an else if chain with && , which is often easier to read.
on an axis
on an axis
Without braces, if (a) if (b) x; else y; attaches the else to the inner if , whatever the indentation suggests. Put braces on every nested if .

title: Sorting three values and the triangle test

text: Right
Obtuse Isosceles
Not triangle After sorting, one test decides each question:
Is it a triangle? a + b > c.
Angle type: compare a² + b² with c². Equal: right. Greater: acute. Smaller: obtuse.
Equilateral: a == c (sorted, so all three equal).
Isosceles: a == b or b == c.
All tests stay in integers, so there is no rounding error. Sorting first removes the "which side is longest" case analysis.
Compute the cost of each choice and keep the minimum. Start the minimum at a value larger than any answer (LLONG_MAX ), or at the first choice. The idea behind P1909.
0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 is false for doubles. Compare with a tolerance, fabs(x - y) < 1e-9 , or better, multiply out so everything stays an integer.
The Luogu problems for this chapter, a ladder through them, and experiments to try yourself.
Key points to memorise
1. Comparisons give bool: true (1) or false (0); any non-zero counts as true.
2. && and || short-circuit: n != 0 && a / n > 2 is safe.
3. 1 < x < 5 is wrong; write 1 < x && x < 5.
4. else-if chains test in order and run only the first true branch.
5. switch: each case needs break; ? : picks one of two values.
6. Nested ifs: braces always; else binds to the nearest if.
8. Sort three with swaps; triangle if a + b > c; compare a²+b² with c² exactly.
